title: Form purpose, action, method (conceptual)
learningObjectives: Use form purpose, action, method (conceptual) correctly and accessibly.

understand.concept: A form collects user input. action identifies the submission destination and method selects how data is sent, commonly GET for retrieval-oriented queries and POST for submissions that change state. A real backend must validate and authorize.
understand.whyItMatters: Correct semantic structure improves meaning, accessibility and maintainability.
understand.analogy: Think of a carefully organised record book.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is limited; browser semantics and accessibility are defined by HTML.

explain.narrative: A form collects user input. action identifies the submission destination and method selects how data is sent, commonly GET for retrieval-oriented queries and POST for submissions that change state. A real backend must validate and authorize.

examples.code: <form action="/search" method="get"><label for="q">Search</label><input id="q" name="q"><button type="submit">Search</button></form>
examples.explanation: Inspect attributes, element nesting and labels. Run the example and modify it in your browser.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser renders the semantic HTML structure.

practise.guidedTask: Modify the data or controls in the example and observe the result.
practise.independentTask: Build a small accessible component using this topic for a realistic course or registration page.
hints: Choose elements for meaning, not appearance.
Client-side validation is not a security boundary.

practice.starterCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>Form purpose, action, method (conceptual)</title></head><body>
<form action="/search" method="get"><label for="q">Search</label><input id="q" name="q"><button type="submit">Search</button></form>
</body></html>

</body></html>

questions.prompt: Which method is commonly used for a search query?
questions.explanation: Choose the semantic element or attribute designed for this role.

questions.prompt: Do client-side HTML checks alone make submitted data trustworthy?
questions.explanation: Trusted server-side validation and authorization are required.
